name: Ford - Sharonville Transmission Plant, Sharonville OH

fieldNotes.location: Roster point landed mid-building; locked center to 39.27229,-84.42525, the centroid of the single large transmission-plant complex on E Sharon Rd. Confirmed via Ford Authority / AmericanAutoWorker as Sharonville Transmission Plant (est. 1958, 10R140/10R80 transmissions).
fieldNotes.truckGate: Fenced truck-yard entrance on the NW side off Mosteller Rd: continuous chain-link perimeter fence, Ford signboard, wide paved apron and gate opening into the trailer-canopy drop yard (Street View 2025-06).
fieldNotes.guardShack: No distinct guard booth resolved at the NW truck gate in z21 satellite or Street View; treated as remote/kiosk check-in (remoteGs true). Low confidence on absence.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: Set true because there is a controlled truck gate but no visible staffed booth.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Large dedicated trailer-storage yard on NW side: dozens of trailers parked under and around canopy structures, plus a second drop area on the SW side.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Dock banks on the SW and N building faces; ~30 doors estimated across faces, regular bay rhythm partially obscured by canopies — band 25-50.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Distinct dock clusters on different building faces (SW truck yard vs N rail-served face) indicate separate shipping/receiving.
fieldNotes.railServed: Rail line runs along the north edge with a spur reaching the building's north face; classic mid-century assembly-area rail service.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide paved gate apron at the NW entrance with ample unused width to add an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Estimated 2 in / 2 out from gate-apron width; not precisely countable from imagery.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Sharonville is inside the Cincinnati metro industrial fabric — Urban.

citations.claim: Ford awarded Sharonville $900M to run current product and introduce 10R80/10R100 transmissions
Oct 2023 layoffs explicitly temporary (UAW strike), confirming Ford operation

verification.rationale: Ford-owned Super Duty transmission plant; 2023 layoffs temporary strike-related, no closure.
